The '''Chicago school of mathematical analysis''' is a [[school of thought]] in mathematics that emphasizes the applications of [[Fourier analysis]] to the study of [[partial differential equations]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Zygmund.html|title=Antoni Zygmund (1900-1992)|website=www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> Mathematician [[Antoni Zygmund]] co-founded the school with his doctoral student [[Alberto Calderón]] at the [[University of Chicago]] in the 1950s.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/20/us/alberto-calderon-77-pioneer-of-mathematical-analysis.html|title=Alberto Calderon, 77, Pioneer Of Mathematical Analysis|last=Noble|first=Holcomb B.|date=1998-04-20|work=The New York Times|access-date=2019-06-22|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1998-04-19-9804190439-story.html|title=ALBERTO CALDERON, MATH GENIUS|last=Warnick|first=Mark S.|website=chicagotribune.com|date=19 April 1998 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1998/04/20/professor-alberto-calderon-77-dies/069850e0-284c-4f03-9ce8-64a7e114274c/|title=PROFESSOR ALBERTO CALDERON, 77, DIES|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=2019-06-22|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}}</ref> Over the years, Zygmund mentored over 40 doctoral students at the University of Chicago.<ref name=":0" />

== Key people ==

* [[Antoni Zygmund]] 
* [[Alberto Calderón]]
*[[Paul Cohen]], [[Fields Medal]] winner (1966)
* [[Charles Fefferman]], [[Fields Medal]] winner (1978)
* [[Eli Stein]]

== Comments ==
The Chicago school of analysis is considered to be one of the strongest schools of mathematical analysis in the 20th century, which was responsible for some of the most important developments in analysis.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> 

== Awards ==
In 1986, Antoni Zygmund received the [[National Medal of Science]], in part for his "creation and leadership of the strongest school of analytical research in the contemporary mathematical world."<ref name="USNSF">{{cite web | title=The President's National Medal of Science: Recipient Details | year=2006 | publisher=The [[National Science Foundation]] | url=https://www.nsf.gov/od/nms/recip_details.cfm?recip_id=411}}</ref>
